architect: Design types, interfaces, and module boundaries before implementation. Use for /architect, architect this, or design this.
arena: Compare competing solutions, choose a base, and incorporate useful parts. Use for /arena, arena this, or design bakeoffs.
automate-me: Capture or update the user's working preferences in a personal mode skill. Use for automate me or create/update my mode skill.
blast-radius: Trace what a change could break beyond its diff. Use for blast radius, what could this break, or reviewing a risky small change.
create-verification-skill: Create a project verification skill that exercises real user behavior. Use for /create-verification-skill or make a control skill for this repo.
figure-it-out: Design an auditable workflow for a large migration or a task without a suitable playbook. Use for /figure-it-out or figure it out.
how: Explain how code works, including runtime flow, placement, ownership, and layering. Use for how does X work or a code walkthrough.
interrogate: Adversarially review changes and report a verdict without applying fixes. Use for interrogate, challenge this, stress test this code, or multi-model review.
maintain-verification-skill: Audit a project verification skill and feature map against source and live behavior. Use for /maintain-verification-skill or audit the verify skill.
make-bot-ui: Explain the unsupported Grok Bot webhook UI workflow. Use for make-bot-ui or a request to build the upstream bot UI.
no-comments: Review comments and replace misleading explanations with clearer code where appropriate. Use for /no-comments or a comment review.
poteto-help: Guide users through Pstack setup, skills, playbooks, and limitations. Use for /poteto-help or Pstack help.
recall: Reconstruct recent in-scope working context. Use for recall my work on X, catch me up, or where did I leave off.
reflect: Review the current conversation for durable lessons and propose skill changes. Use when the user says reflect or /reflect.
setup-pstack: Configure Pstack for the capabilities actually available in this host. Use for /setup-pstack, configure pstack models, or pstack budget.
show-me-your-work: Keep a reviewable decision trail for long or multi-phase work. Use for /show-me-your-work or work reviewed later.
swarm: Coordinate coverage, races, or exploration across available workers. Use for /swarm, swarm this, or parallel coverage.
why: Investigate why code or a design exists using available evidence. Use for why does X work this way, design rationale, regressions, or postmortems.
principle-guard-the-context-window: Manage large context and outputs without losing evidence. Apply when context is filling up.
principle-never-block-on-the-human: Proceed with authorized reversible work while respecting scope and approval boundaries. Apply when considering an unnecessary permission question.
